bass.name: Bass
bass.description: A popular freshwater game fish known for its fighting spirit when caught.
bass.diet: Smaller fish, insects, and aquatic creatures
bass.funFact: Bass can live up to 15 years and are very protective of their nests during spawning season.

blobfish.name: Blobfish
blobfish.description: A deep-sea fish that looks very different when brought to the surface due to pressure changes.
blobfish.diet: Small crustaceans and organic matter floating in the water
blobfish.funFact: The blobfish was voted the 'world's ugliest animal' but only looks blob-like out of water!

butterfly_fish.name: Butterfly Fish
butterfly_fish.description: Colorful tropical fish with beautiful patterns, popular in aquariums.
butterfly_fish.habitat: Coral reefs in warm tropical waters
butterfly_fish.diet: Coral polyps, algae, and small invertebrates
butterfly_fish.funFact: Butterfly fish often mate for life and swim in pairs around coral reefs.

catfish.name: Catfish
catfish.description: Freshwater fish with whisker-like barbels that help them find food in murky water.
catfish.size: Varies greatly, from 4 inches to over 8 feet
catfish.diet: Bottom feeders eating plants, insects, and small fish
catfish.funFact: Catfish have over 100,000 taste buds all over their body, not just in their mouth!

char.name: Char
char.description: A cold-water fish related to salmon and trout, prized for its delicate flavor.
char.habitat: Cold lakes and streams in northern regions
char.diet: Insects, small fish, and aquatic invertebrates
char.funFact: Arctic char can survive in water so cold it's almost freezing and can change color based on their environment.

cherry_salmon.name: Cherry Salmon
cherry_salmon.description: A Pacific salmon species known for its beautiful pink coloration during spawning.
cherry_salmon.habitat: Pacific Ocean and rivers in Japan, Korea, and Russia
cherry_salmon.diet: Small fish, squid, and crustaceans in the ocean
cherry_salmon.funFact: Cherry salmon get their name from their cherry-blossom pink color during mating season.

clown_fish.name: Clownfish
clown_fish.description: Bright orange fish with white stripes, famous for living in sea anemones.
clown_fish.habitat: Coral reefs in the Indo-Pacific region
clown_fish.funFact: Clownfish are immune to sea anemone stings and help clean the anemone in exchange for protection!

cod.name: Cod
cod.description: An important commercial fish with flaky white meat, found in cold northern waters.
cod.habitat: North Atlantic and Pacific cold waters
cod.size: 2-6 feet long, can weigh up to 200 pounds
cod.diet: Small fish, crabs, worms, and mollusks
cod.funFact: Cod can live up to 25 years and were so important to early American economy that a wooden cod hangs in the Massachusetts State House!

coho_salmon.name: Coho Salmon
coho_salmon.description: Also known as silver salmon, these fish are born in freshwater but live most of their adult life in the ocean.
coho_salmon.funFact: Coho salmon can jump up to 10 feet high to clear obstacles when swimming upstream to spawn!

cow_fish.name: Cowfish
cow_fish.description: A box-shaped fish with horn-like projections that look like a cow's horns.
cow_fish.diet: Algae, small crustaceans, and organic matter
cow_fish.funFact: Cowfish can release toxins when stressed, which is why they're challenging to keep in aquariums with other fish.

giant_tevally.name: Giant Trevally
giant_tevally.description: A large, powerful predator fish known for its incredible hunting abilities.
giant_tevally.size: Can grow up to 5 feet and weigh 150 pounds
giant_tevally.funFact: Giant trevally have been filmed jumping out of the water to catch birds flying overhead!

golden_trout.name: Golden Trout
golden_trout.description: California's state fish, known for its beautiful golden color and red markings.
golden_trout.habitat: High mountain streams and lakes in the Sierra Nevada
golden_trout.diet: Insects, small crustaceans, and aquatic larvae
golden_trout.funFact: Golden trout live at elevations above 10,000 feet and can survive in very cold, oxygen-poor water.

guppy.name: Guppy
guppy.description: Small, colorful tropical fish popular in home aquariums.
guppy.habitat: Freshwater streams in South America, now worldwide in aquariums
guppy.diet: Small insects, plant matter, and fish flakes in aquariums
guppy.funFact: Female guppies can store sperm for up to 8 months and give birth to live babies instead of laying eggs!

halibut.name: Halibut
halibut.description: One of the largest flatfish, with both eyes on one side of their head.
halibut.habitat: Ocean floors in the North Pacific and Atlantic
halibut.size: Can grow up to 8 feet and weigh over 400 pounds
halibut.diet: Fish, crabs, squid, and other bottom-dwelling creatures
halibut.funFact: Halibut start life swimming upright like normal fish, but one eye migrates to the other side as they grow!

herring.name: Herring
herring.description: Small, silver fish that swim in huge schools and are important food for many marine animals.
herring.habitat: Coastal waters of the North Atlantic and Pacific
herring.diet: Plankton, small crustaceans, and fish larvae
herring.funFact: Herring schools can contain millions of fish and create underwater 'bait balls' that attract whales, dolphins, and seabirds.

lion_fish.name: Lionfish
lion_fish.description: Beautiful but venomous fish with flowing fins that look like a lion's mane.
lion_fish.habitat: Indo-Pacific coral reefs, invasive in Atlantic waters
lion_fish.funFact: Lionfish have venomous spines that can cause painful stings to humans, but they're not naturally aggressive.

loach.name: Loach
loach.description: Bottom-dwelling freshwater fish with barbels around their mouth for finding food.
loach.diet: Insects, worms, and organic matter on the bottom
loach.funFact: Some loaches can predict weather changes and become more active before storms!

mackerel.name: Mackerel
mackerel.description: Fast-swimming fish with distinctive tiger-like stripes on their back.
mackerel.funFact: Mackerel can swim up to 35 mph and must keep moving constantly to breathe properly.

mahi_mahi.name: Mahi Mahi
mahi_mahi.description: Also called dolphinfish, these colorful fish are prized for sport fishing and eating.
mahi_mahi.size: 3-6 feet long, can weigh up to 90 pounds
mahi_mahi.diet: Flying fish, squid, crabs, and other fish
mahi_mahi.funFact: Mahi mahi can change colors rapidly when excited or stressed, flashing bright blues, greens, and yellows!

manta_ray.name: Manta Ray
manta_ray.description: Giant, graceful rays that glide through the ocean like underwater birds.
manta_ray.size: Can have a wingspan up to 29 feet!
manta_ray.diet: Plankton, small fish, and tiny crustaceans
manta_ray.funFact: Manta rays have the largest brain of any fish and are known to recognize themselves in mirrors!

napolean_fish.name: Napoleon Fish
napolean_fish.description: Also called humphead wrasse, these are massive reef fish with a distinctive forehead bump.
napolean_fish.size: Can grow up to 7 feet and weigh 400 pounds
napolean_fish.diet: Fish, mollusks, crustaceans, and sea urchins
napolean_fish.funFact: Napoleon fish can live over 30 years and all start life as females before some change to males!

neon_tetras.name: Neon Tetras
neon_tetras.description: Tiny, brilliantly colored fish with electric blue and red stripes.
neon_tetras.habitat: Amazon Basin rivers in South America
neon_tetras.diet: Small insects, worms, and plant matter
neon_tetras.funFact: Neon tetras' bright colors fade at night when they sleep to help them hide from predators.

oarfish.name: Oarfish
oarfish.description: The world's longest bony fish, sometimes called the 'sea serpent' due to its ribbon-like body.
oarfish.size: Can grow up to 36 feet long!
oarfish.funFact: Oarfish usually live so deep they're rarely seen alive, leading to sea monster legends when they wash ashore.

ocean_sunfish.name: Ocean Sunfish
ocean_sunfish.description: The world's heaviest bony fish, with a unique flat, round shape.
ocean_sunfish.size: Can weigh up to 5,000 pounds and be 14 feet long
ocean_sunfish.funFact: Ocean sunfish can lay up to 300 million eggs at once - more than any other vertebrate!

parrot_fish.name: Parrotfish
parrot_fish.description: Colorful reef fish with beak-like mouths that crunch coral to eat algae.
parrot_fish.diet: Algae growing on coral and rocks
parrot_fish.funFact: Parrotfish poop creates tropical beaches! They eat coral and excrete sand - up to 840 pounds per fish per year.

pike.name: Pike
pike.description: Aggressive freshwater predator with a long body and sharp teeth.
pike.habitat: Lakes and slow rivers in northern regions
pike.size: 2-5 feet long, can weigh up to 60 pounds
pike.diet: Fish, frogs, ducklings, and other aquatic animals
pike.funFact: Pike can live up to 75 years and are ambush predators that can accelerate from 0 to 25 mph instantly!

pink_salmon.name: Pink Salmon
pink_salmon.description: The smallest Pacific salmon, also called humpback salmon due to males' spawning hump.
pink_salmon.habitat: North Pacific Ocean and connected rivers
pink_salmon.funFact: Pink salmon have a strict 2-year life cycle and all return to spawn in odd or even years depending on their population.

pirana.name: Piranha
pirana.description: Sharp-toothed fish from South America, famous for their powerful bite.
pirana.habitat: Rivers and lakes in the Amazon Basin
pirana.diet: Fish, insects, plants, and occasionally larger animals
pirana.funFact: Most piranhas are actually vegetarians! Only a few species are the aggressive carnivores shown in movies.

plaice.name: Plaice
plaice.description: A flatfish with orange spots that lives on sandy ocean floors.
plaice.habitat: Sandy bottoms of the North Sea and Atlantic
plaice.funFact: Plaice can change their color and pattern to match the sea floor where they're hiding!

pompano.name: Pompano
pompano.description: Silver, disc-shaped fish prized for their delicious taste and fighting ability.
pompano.habitat: Warm coastal waters, especially around reefs
pompano.funFact: Pompano are considered one of the best-tasting fish in the ocean and can live up to 8 years.

puffer_fish.name: Pufferfish
puffer_fish.description: Round fish that can inflate their body like a balloon when threatened.
puffer_fish.size: 1 inch to 2 feet depending on species
puffer_fish.diet: Algae, small invertebrates, and sometimes coral
puffer_fish.funFact: Pufferfish contain a powerful toxin called tetrodotoxin that's 1,200 times more poisonous than cyanide!

rainbow_fish.name: Rainbow Fish
rainbow_fish.description: Brightly colored freshwater fish popular in aquariums for their shimmering scales.
rainbow_fish.habitat: Rivers and lakes in Australia and New Guinea
rainbow_fish.diet: Small insects, worms, and plant matter
rainbow_fish.funFact: Rainbow fish get their name from their iridescent scales that reflect light like a rainbow!

sea_horse.name: Seahorse
sea_horse.description: Unique fish with a horse-like head that swims upright and has a prehensile tail.
sea_horse.habitat: Shallow tropical and temperate coastal waters
sea_horse.funFact: Male seahorses are the only male animals that get pregnant and give birth to babies!

shark_greatwhite.name: Great White Shark
shark_greatwhite.description: The ocean's apex predator, famous for its size and powerful bite.
shark_greatwhite.habitat: Coastal waters worldwide, especially cooler regions
shark_greatwhite.size: 15-26 feet long, can weigh over 5,000 pounds
shark_greatwhite.diet: Seals, sea lions, fish, and occasionally sea turtles
shark_greatwhite.funFact: Great whites can detect a single drop of blood in 25 gallons of water and live up to 70 years!

shark_hammerhead.name: Hammerhead Shark
shark_hammerhead.description: Distinctive shark with a flattened head shaped like a hammer.
shark_hammerhead.funFact: The hammer-shaped head gives them 360-degree vision and helps them detect electrical signals from prey!

shark_saw.name: Sawshark
shark_saw.description: Shark with a long, flat snout lined with sharp teeth like a saw blade.
shark_saw.habitat: Deep waters of the Indo-Pacific and Atlantic
shark_saw.funFact: Sawsharks use their saw-like snout to slash through schools of fish and detect buried prey with electrical sensors!

shark_whale.name: Whale Shark
shark_whale.description: The world's largest fish, but gentle giants that eat only tiny plankton.
shark_whale.size: Can grow up to 40 feet long and weigh 20 tons
shark_whale.diet: Plankton, small fish, and fish eggs
shark_whale.funFact: Despite being the biggest fish, whale sharks are completely harmless to humans and often let divers swim alongside them!

silver_eel.name: Silver Eel
silver_eel.description: Long, snake-like fish that can live in both fresh and salt water.
silver_eel.habitat: Rivers and lakes, migrating to ocean to spawn
silver_eel.funFact: Silver eels can live up to 85 years and migrate thousands of miles to the Sargasso Sea to spawn!

sockeye_salmon.name: Sockeye Salmon
sockeye_salmon.description: Pacific salmon known for turning bright red with green heads during spawning season.
sockeye_salmon.habitat: North Pacific Ocean and connected rivers
sockeye_salmon.funFact: Sockeye salmon can navigate back to the exact stream where they were born using their sense of smell!

squid.name: Squid
squid.description: Intelligent marine animal with ten arms, two tentacles, and the ability to change color.
squid.habitat: Oceans worldwide, from surface to deep water
squid.size: 1 inch to 43 feet depending on species
squid.funFact: Squid have three hearts, blue blood, and can shoot ink clouds to escape predators!

sucker_fish.name: Suckerfish
sucker_fish.description: Fish with a disc-shaped mouth that attaches to larger animals for transportation.
sucker_fish.size: 6 inches to 3 feet depending on species
sucker_fish.diet: Parasites and dead skin from host animals
sucker_fish.funFact: Suckerfish help clean sharks and other large fish, creating a win-win relationship called symbiosis!

surgeon_fish.name: Surgeonfish
surgeon_fish.description: Colorful reef fish with sharp, scalpel-like spines on their tails.
surgeon_fish.diet: Algae growing on rocks and coral
surgeon_fish.funFact: Surgeonfish got their name from the razor-sharp spines that can cut like a surgeon's scalpel!

swordfish.name: Swordfish
swordfish.description: Large, fast fish with a long, flat bill resembling a sword.
swordfish.size: 6-14 feet long, can weigh up to 1,400 pounds
swordfish.funFact: Swordfish can swim up to 60 mph and use their sword to stun prey by slashing through schools of fish!

whiting_fish.name: Whiting
whiting_fish.description: Small to medium-sized fish related to cod, popular for eating.
whiting_fish.habitat: Coastal waters of the Atlantic and Pacific
whiting_fish.funFact: Whiting are an important commercial fish and are often used in fish and chips because of their mild, flaky meat.
